questions.enonce_markdown:
6. (a) Why was Apartheid introduced in South Africa in 1948?

**(7 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Apartheid** ("apartness" in Afrikaans) was the system of racial segregation and white minority rule introduced by the **National Party** after it won the general election of **May 1948** under **D. F. Malan**, and it lasted until 1994.

**Reasons (7 marks, 1 mark each).**
- **Afrikaner nationalism.** The Afrikaners, descendants of the Dutch settlers, wanted to protect their language, culture and power against British influence and against the African majority; the Dutch Reformed Church supported the idea of separate development.
- **Fear of the black majority** ("swart gevaar"): whites were a small minority and feared losing political and economic power as Africans grew in number and moved to the towns.
- **Urbanisation of Africans.** During the war many Africans moved to the cities to work in industry, and whites wanted to control them with stricter laws.
- **Economic reasons.** The Afrikaner "poor whites" needed jobs and protection against African competition; apartheid kept cheap black labour for the mines, farms and factories and reserved the best jobs and land for whites.
- **The tradition of segregation.** Laws like the **Natives Land Act of 1913** and the laws of 1936 had already separated the races; apartheid extended and made them stricter.
- **The 1948 election result.** The National Party won with the slogan of apartheid, having promised to protect white supremacy, and had the power to pass the laws.
- **Fear of communism and of the demands of African and Indian groups** after the Second World War, and the example of decolonisation elsewhere, which made the white government more determined.

**Conclusion.** Apartheid was introduced to keep Afrikaner and white power, protect white economic interests and control the black majority.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Show how Apartheid was practised in South Africa as a system of government between 1948 and 1994?

**(7 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Apartheid was applied through a large number of laws that divided South Africans by race and gave white people power and privilege.

**How apartheid was practised (7 marks, 1 mark each).**
- **Racial classification.** The **Population Registration Act (1950)** classified everyone as White, Black (African), Coloured or Indian (Asian).
- **Separate living areas.** The **Group Areas Act (1950)** reserved areas for each race and led to forced removals (for example Sophiatown in the 1950s and District Six in Cape Town later).
- **Ban on mixed marriages and sexual relations** between races (the **Prohibition of Mixed Marriages Act of 1949** and the **Immorality Act**).
- **Pass laws.** Africans had to carry passes (the "dompas") and could be arrested if they were in a white area without permission.
- **Petty apartheid.** The **Reservation of Separate Amenities Act (1953)** separated beaches, buses, schools, hospitals and public places.
- **Inferior education.** The **Bantu Education Act (1953)** gave Africans a separate education aimed at manual work.
- **Bantustans (homelands).** The **Promotion of Bantu Self-Government Act (1959)** and later laws created ten homelands, such as Transkei and Bophuthatswana, and took away South African citizenship from Africans.
- **Political exclusion and repression.** Black people had no vote in national elections; the **Suppression of Communism Act (1950)** and later laws were used against opponents; the **Sharpeville massacre (21 March 1960)**, the banning of the ANC and PAC (1960), the **Rivonia Trial (1963-1964)** that sent Mandela and others to prison, the **Soweto uprising of 16 June 1976**, the death of **Steve Biko** in 1977 and the states of emergency of the 1980s showed the violence of the system.

**Conclusion.** Apartheid was a system of government in which race decided where people lived, worked, studied and voted, kept in place by laws, police and army.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Describe the contributions of ANC to the establishment of Black Majority rule in South Africa in 1994.

**(6 marks)**
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The **African National Congress (ANC)**, founded in 1912 as the South African Native National Congress, led the struggle against white domination and became the governing party after the first non-racial elections of **27 April 1994**.

**Contributions (6 marks, 1 mark each).**
- **Peaceful protest and campaigns.** The ANC led the **Defiance Campaign of 1952** against unjust laws, and organised strikes, boycotts and demonstrations against the pass laws.
- **The Freedom Charter (1955).** The Congress of the People adopted the Charter at Kliptown, which set out the demand for a non-racial, democratic South Africa and became the programme of the movement.
- **Armed struggle.** After the ban of 1960 the ANC formed **Umkhonto we Sizwe (1961)** under Nelson Mandela, to attack government and economic targets.
- **Leadership and sacrifice.** Leaders such as **Nelson Mandela, Walter Sisulu and Oliver Tambo** were imprisoned or went into exile; **Mandela's long imprisonment (from 1962 to 1990, mostly on Robben Island)** made him a world symbol, and the ANC in exile built support abroad.
- **International pressure.** The ANC and its allies led the campaigns for **sanctions and boycotts** (including sport), and won the support of the UN, the OAU and many countries, which isolated the apartheid government; internally the **United Democratic Front** and trade unions (such as COSATU) organised mass resistance in the 1980s.
- **Negotiations.** The ANC was unbanned in **February 1990** and Mandela was freed on 11 February 1990; the ANC negotiated with President **F. W. de Klerk** (CODESA, 1991-1993) a new constitution with equal rights.
- **Election victory.** The ANC won the elections of April 1994 and **Mandela became the first Black President** in May 1994.

**Conclusion.** Through protest, armed struggle, international campaigns and negotiation the ANC brought about Black majority rule in 1994.
